turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on through, grab a seat. I've got the nurse's slip here, just give me a tick.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Thank you for seeing me today.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Morning. I'm Ellen, his support worker. I bring him to his appointments.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good on you. So, what's brought you in?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): I have come about a lump in my groin. It has been on my mind.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Which side is it on?
[SEG0007] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He nearly stayed home, said it would settle, but I—
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): The right side, doctor. Forgive me for cutting across.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long have you noticed it?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I would put it at about three months. Well, actually, early February, if I am being precise.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): It appears when I lift something, and it goes away when I lie down.
[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's back on the cement bags this week, even after I said—
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I am a labourer, doctor. The work requires lifting. I know that is not ideal.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain with it, or only the lump?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): There is a mild ache by the evening. Through the day I scarcely notice it.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting? Or nausea alongside it?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I have not vomited, and I have not felt sick.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Waking hot, or shivery?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing of that sort.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your weight? Has it fallen away?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, I am not certain, doctor. Perhaps a little about the waist, though I could not tell you when that began, if it has begun at all.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): How are the bowels? Any change in the habit?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. They remain quite regular.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Righto. The nurse has put blood pressure one oh nine over seventy-seven, pulse eighty-eight, temperature thirty-six point eight, and weight sixty-eight kilos.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Uh, the pulse is off. She said seventy-two today. I watched her write it. Eighty-eight is the old card.

[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Err, yep, wrong line. Pulse is seventy-two, and weight today is seventy-eight point four kilos. Last time in March you were sixty-eight, and your last pressure was one-forty over eighty-eight. We'll use today's figures.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sorry, before that, yesterday the lump actually—
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hang on, let him answer.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. No, doctor, I have never smoked.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ta. Yesterday, then.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It came right out and he couldn't push it back for a good twenty minutes. He went quite pale on the lounge.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): That is correct. I lay down, and in time it returned. There was no vomiting.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. What medicines are you taking just now?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I take metforman for my diabetes. Five hundred milligrams, by mouth, twice a day.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Metformin, yes. That's type 2 diabetes, still ongoing?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. It has been for some years, and I take the tablet as prescribed.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything for the ache?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I had been using ibuprofen, four hundred milligrams when the ache was troublesome. I stopped it a fortnight ago, as it was upsetting my stomach.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I am aware of, doctor.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll have a look, if you lie back for me. There is a soft swelling in the right groin, and it reduces when you lie flat. I can feel a cough impulse. The abdomen is soft, with no tenderness.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thinking aloud. A lump that comes out on lifting and goes back on lying down, with a cough impulse, in a man doing heavy work. My working impression is a right inguinal hernia. Not the final word, the surgeon might frame it differently, but that is where I land.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. What do you propose?
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): I was going to book an ultrasound and review you in six weeks, as long as it kept reducing easily.
[SEG0047] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He's on the tools Monday, doctor, and yesterday it stuck. Six weeks is—

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. You're right, that new bit changes it. Scrap the ultrasound, and scrap the six-week wait. I'll refer you to general surgery at the public hospital so they can see you and talk about a repair.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): I would be most grateful. Should I stop the lifting in the meantime?

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. No heavy lifting, and no cement bags, until the surgeons have seen you. If it comes out, lie down and ease it back gently. If it will not go back, or the pain turns severe, or you begin vomiting, go to emergency and don't wait.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand, doctor, and I will follow that.
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll see you back here in four weeks, so we can check it hasn't changed, whether or not the surgical clinic has come through. The referral goes today.

spec.situation: Manual worker with a groin lump that appears on lifting and goes away lying down; mild ache by evening; no vomiting; surgical referral planned, advice on lifting.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Caregiver reports 20 minutes yesterday and lying down helped; right groin not explicitly stated by caregiver.
bad.text: Irreducible groin lump (category=other, status=resolved, duration=approximately 20 minutes, onset=yesterday, temporality=resolved, body_site=right groin, relieving_factors=lying down, reported_by=caregiver, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Weight loss is recorded incorrectly: the patient was unsure whether any weight loss had occurred ('perhaps a little about the waist... if it has begun at all'), so weight loss should not be recorded as present.
Caregiver reported that during yesterday's episode when the lump would not reduce for about 20 minutes, the patient went quite pale.
Ibuprofen was stopped a fortnight ago because it was upsetting his stomach.
The initial plan discussed was ultrasound and review in six weeks if the lump kept reducing easily, but this plan was explicitly changed after hearing about the stuck lump.
Doctor stated the referral to general surgery goes today.
